evidence.text: It is incorrectly called the principle of least time
there will be no first-order change in the time

Editorial summary of section 26-6, not a direct quotation: The photon-arrival probability is calculated by summing complex amplitude contributions over available paths and squaring the resulting magnitude. In the mirror example, paths near a stationary travel time supply nearly aligned contributions; widely differing phases largely cancel. This is a sum over amplitudes, not a claim that only one mathematically exact minimum-time path contributes.

Editorial summary of section 26-1, not a direct quotation: Geometrical optics is an approximation for suitable scale and sensitivity conditions. The chapter distinguishes this approximation from wave behavior and the fuller quantum description.

claims.claim_text: Light explores every available route from point A to point B rather than selecting one route.
claims.review_note: The creator uses literal-sounding language; a response should not equate the mathematical path sum with experimentally established literal trajectories.

claims.claim_text: Quantum interference means that only the route taking the least time ends up contributing to light propagation.
claims.review_note: Paraphrase of the visible description. Assess simplification and scope; no human truth label assigned.
